naive.label: Naive Forecast
naive.description: Forecast the next period as equal to the most recent observation. Best for white-noise / no-trend data; baseline against which all others are judged.

moving-average.label: Moving Average
moving-average.description: Average of the last n observations. Smooths short-term noise; lags trends.

n.description: Number of most-recent periods to average.

weighted-moving-average.label: Weighted Moving Average
weighted-moving-average.description: Like Moving Average but with explicit weights summing to 1 (most-recent first). Lets the forecaster emphasise recent periods.

weights.description: Array of weights; weights[0] applies to the most-recent observation. Must sum to 1.0 within ±0.001.

exponential-smoothing.label: Exponential Smoothing
exponential-smoothing.description: Recursive weighted average with smoothing constant α. Higher α tracks recent changes faster; lower α produces a smoother forecast.

holts-double-es.label: Holt's Double Exponential Smoothing
holts-double-es.description: Two smoothing constants — α for the level, β for the trend — so the method captures linear trend.

linear-regression.label: Linear Regression
linear-regression.formula: F(t) = a + b·t,   b = Σ(t-t̄)(A-Ā)/Σ(t-t̄)²,   a = Ā - b·t̄
linear-regression.description: Fit a least-squares line over all available history (full-cumulative). Best for clean linear trend; extrapolates linearly. A windowed variant is on the DF-2b backlog.
